title: Nasty Adversarial Training: A Probability Sparsity Perspective for Robustness Enhancement
claim: Training a target model against a shared-backbone adversary counterpart, by maximizing output divergence, turns single-peak predictions into multi-peak distributions.
layout: Dashed method box left, stacked distribution panels right, left-to-right flow
description: The left side is a large dashed box holding the training pipeline. Clean and adversarial cat images are stacked in a small dashed group, with green and red borders. Hollow arrows lead from them to two neural-network icons: the Target Model on top and the Adversary Counterpart below. A 'Share Backbone' box links the two networks. Each network outputs a column of colored logit circles. A 'Maximize Similarity' box connects the target logits to a stacked-color Ground Truth bar. A 'Minimize Similarity' box sits between the target logits and the adversarial logits. The right side stacks three panels. A single-peak bar histogram sits at the top, a 'Probabilistic rectification' box with curved arrows sits in the middle, and a multi-peak histogram sits at the bottom. Pastel fills and large serif labels dominate, and the eye starts at the cat images.
caption: Framework of the proposed NAT. NAT enhances the target model’s training by introducing an auxiliary adversary model in addition to the primary training loss. Probability sparsity regularization (i.e., probabilistic rectification) is achieved by maximizing the divergence between the output distributions of the target model and the adversary model.
abstract: The vulnerability of deep neural networks to adversarial examples poses significant challenges to their reliable deployment. Among existing empirical defenses, adversarial training and robust distillation have proven the most effective. In this paper, we identify a property originally associated with model intellectual property, i.e., probability sparsity induced by nasty training, and demonstrate that it can also provide interpretable improvements to adversarial robustness. We begin by analyzing how nasty training induces sparse probability distributions and qualitatively explore the spatial metric preferences this sparsity introduces to the model. Building on these insights, we propose a simple yet effective adversarial training method, nasty adversarial training (NAT), which incorporates probability sparsity as a regularization mechanism to boost adversarial robustness. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results validate the effectiveness of NAT, highlighting its potential to enhance the adversarial robustness of deep neural networks in an interpretable manner.
